data.title: Redox-sensitive mTOR-eIF4A signaling promotes selective P-glycoprotein translation.
data.authors: Jin P; Jin M; Feng L; He J; Ying Y; Bai R et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Oxidative stress activates a redox-sensitive PI3K-AKT-mTORC1-eIF4A cascade that selectively promotes P-glycoprotein translation via cap-dependent mRNA engagement, revealing a transcription-independent mechanism of rapid multidrug resistance induction.
data.abstract_excerpt: Cells face a temporal gap in oxidative stress adaptation, in which acute insults require rapid protein synthesis before transcriptional responses are fully established. Low-dose glucosamine (GlcN) induces a transient intracellular oxidation-sensitive response and activates redox-sensitive PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 signaling, leading to increased P-glycoprotein (P-gp) abundance without a detectable increase in total ABCB1 mRNA.

extracted_findings.effect: mTOR-eIF4A selectively upregulates P-gp translation under oxidative stress; multidrug resistance
